Generate proposed edits only for affected sections, with evidence-backed explanations and conflict handling for concurrent author edits.

**User outcome:** “Show which conclusions in last month's report need revisiting after this correction.” The user gets a focused proposed revision and can inspect exactly why it changed.

**Existing foundation:** `src/kb/artifacts.py`, `claim_timelines.py`, `change_briefs.py`, `citation_preservation.py`, and `research_packages.py`. Change briefs already summarize supplied before/after states. The proposed addition is an authored report whose sections and assertions have durable dependency links and a revision workflow.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] users accept/reject individual proposals; accepted changes create a versioned report, while earlier reports remain reproducible.
- [ ] Export the updated report and bibliography without automatically publishing it externally.

Code and evidence pointers (reviewed revision):

- [src/kb/artifacts.py](https://github.com/Ikey168/Noesis/blob/0bf70327/src/kb/artifacts.py)
- [src/kb/change_briefs.py](https://github.com/Ikey168/Noesis/blob/0bf70327/src/kb/change_briefs.py)

Validation: exercise the acceptance scenarios through the supported public contract/API, including relevant replay, access, and unavailable-input cases. Preserve evidence identity and explicit uncertainty; do not count synthetic fixtures as real-world validation.

Add explicit optional backends for dimensional formula evaluation and robust geometry operations.

Pint carries versioned Noesis units through bounded arithmetic and validates the output dimension. Receipts preserve unit/observation/formula identities, exact Decimal literals and half-even rounding. Nine authored exact-arithmetic cases compare native/Pint values and operating cost. Offset formulas require explicit conversion; economic provenance and native defaults remain unchanged.

Shapely adds projected topology-preserving simplification through the existing geometry/MCP surfaces and a v2 contract for MultiPolygon. It retains originals and pyproj receipts, propagates declared precision, rejects automatic repairs/unsupported CRS/dateline operations, and checks sampled displacement. Analytic reference shapes and an actual ALKIS Berlin Mitte boundary validate topology and compare native/Shapely simplification. Full evidence and native fixtures are included.

Validation: 96 integration/quantitative/catalog tests and 94 integration/geospatial/catalog tests passed; focused tests cover actual MCP options and authorization. Ruff and whitespace checks passed. The native Berlin comparison retained valid topology, reducing 2,555 coordinates to 222; measured cost and sampling limits are documented.
